newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Air Afrique says crashed Boeing 737 a writeoff.
newsitem.headline: Air Afrique says crashed Boeing 737 a writeoff.

text.p: An Air Afrique Boeing 737 which was gutted by fire after crashing in Cameroon will have to be written off, the company said.
"I think it is a write-off," Air Afrique Director-General Sir Harry Tirvengadum told Reuters in an interview on Tuesday. He said more than 70 percent of the plane was destroyed by fire.
Tirvengadum said the plane was fully insured "by several compnaies", but he had no immediate details of the assurers or the aircraft's year of manufacture.

None of the 117 passengers and crew was seriously hurt when the plane aborted a takeoff and crashed at Douala airport in Cameroon on Sunday night. Emergency services managed to evacuate all on board before fire engulfed the plane. The baggage was untouched by the fire.
Fifteen passengers were treated in hospital for minor injuries.
Tirvengadum, who took charge at the debt-ridden multinational carrier's Abidjan headquarters last February, praised the professionalism of the pilot.
Crew members said the pilot averted a disaster after a tyre on one of the plane's undercarriage burst as it took off for N'Djamena, Chad, via Bangui in the Central African Republic.

"From what the captain told me, he thinks he hit something on the runway and the tyre burst," Tirvengadum said, adding however, that investigators were trying to establish the real cause of the crash.
Investigators from Air Afrique and the civil aviation authorities of Cameroon and Ivory Coast were on the scene.
The flight originated in Abidjan with a stop in the Togolese capital Lome.
